raw_case_text:
A 65-year-old male presented with single, painful, non-healing ulcer on the right sole with multiple, pink verrucous nodules at the lateral margin of the ulcer, involving the right lateral malleolus and lateral border of the right sole since two years. On detailed history taking, it was revealed that two years ago, patient had a traumatic injury on his right sole for which he did not consult any registered medical practitioner and applied some homemade chemicals on the wound. Surgical intervention was done to debride the wound by local, untrained, nonmedical personnel without proper antibiotic coverage, which led to secondary infections and nonhealing ulceration. Within the next 6 months, after developing a fully-formed ulcer, multiple small pinkish nodular lesions appeared at the lateral margin of the ulcer, which increased in size with time, coalesced with other nodular lesions, and became verrucous. On local cutaneous examination, a deep seated ulcer of 6 cm x 4 cm x 2 cm size was seen over the right sole, whose floor was clean (because of previous antiseptic cleaning) and the margin was hyperkeratotic and macerated [Figure 1]. Along the lateral border and on the lateral malleolus of right foot, multiple, coalescing, firm, pink-coloured verrucous nodules of varying sizes (largest measuring 3 cm x 2.5 cm) in a "Streusel-bread"-like appearance were present [Figure 2]. The size of the whole coalescing multinodular lesion was 9 cm x 6 cm. There was no regional lymphadenopathy, no loss of sensation, nerve thickening, or any other cutaneous signs of leprosy. There was no clinical or radiological evidence of osteomyelitis. The family history, past medical history, routine laboratory investigations, and systemic examinations were non-contributory.
To reach a final diagnosis, a wedge-shaped incisional biopsy was performed and the sample was sent for histopathological evaluation, which demonstrated vertically oriented, multiple, thin, anastomosing strands centred around the acrosyringium [Figures 3 and 4] forming a lattice of double-layered acrosyringeal ductal structures embedded in delicate fibrovascular stroma, extending into the reticular dermis [Figure 5].
On the basis of detailed history, clinical presentations, and distinct histopathological features, diagnosis of ESFA was made, and it was considered to be reactive in nature due to the traumatic nonhealing ulcer.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 65-year-old male presented with a 2-year history of a painful non-healing ulcer on his right sole bordered laterally by coalescing pink verrucous nodules.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Two years prior to presentation, the patient sustained a traumatic wound on his right sole, applied homemade chemical concoctions, and underwent unsterile debridement by untrained nonmedical personnel without antibiotics, resulting in secondary infection and a chronic non-healing plantar ulcer. Six months after ulcer formation, small pink nodules appeared along the lateral ulcer margin and progressively enlarged and coalesced over 18 months into a verrucous multinodular mass extending to the right lateral malleolus.
subjective.past_medical_history: History of right plantar trauma and unsterile local debridement 2 years prior; otherwise non-contributory medical and family history.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for chronic right plantar ulcer pain; negative for sensory loss or systemic symptoms.

objective.physical_examination: Local cutaneous examination revealed a deep 6 x 4 x 2 cm ulcer on the right sole with a clean floor and macerated, hyperkeratotic margins, bordered along the lateral sole and right lateral malleolus by a 9 x 6 cm coalescing plaque of firm, pink verrucous nodules (largest 3 x 2.5 cm) with a 'Streusel-bread'-like appearance. Cutaneous sensation was intact, peripheral nerves were not thickened, regional lymph nodes were not enlarged, and systemic examination was normal.
objective.routine_investigations: Routine hematological and biochemical investigations and foot radiographs (showing no osteomyelitis) were normal.
objective.advanced_workup: A wedge-shaped incisional biopsy of the verrucous marginal lesion was performed for histopathological evaluation.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Histopathology demonstrated multiple thin, vertically oriented, anastomosing epithelial strands centered around the acrosyringium forming a lattice of double-layered acrosyringeal ductal structures within a delicate fibrovascular stroma extending into the reticular dermis, confirming reactive eccrine syringofibroadenoma (ESFA) secondary to a chronic traumatic plantar ulcer (and excluding leprosy and squamous cell carcinoma).
